title: Dedicated: Autoscaling policies, burst controls, throughput guarantees and utilization reporting
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds configurable autoscaling policy types for Dedicated fleets, burst quota controls, and new utilization reporting metrics and dashboards. Backward compatible; requires operator rollout for new config fields.
description: Context: We need better control over Dedicated fleet scaling to meet throughput guarantees while limiting cost and noisy scaling events. This PR introduces new autoscaling policy primitives (target_utilization, min_capacity, max_capacity, max_scale_per_minute), a burst_quota system to allow controlled short-term over-provisioning, and improved utilization reporting for operator visibility. Motivation: customers running steady low-latency workloads requested deterministic throughput guarantees and fewer transient scale oscillations. This is work for ENG-4521 and supports on-call runbooks for SUP-1284. Summary of changes: - API: add AutoscalingPolicy message to api/dedicated/v1/autoscaling.proto and extend FleetConfig with optional "autoscaling_policy_v2". This is additive and backward compatible. - Controller: implement continuous scaling loop in go/services/fleet/autoscaler.go with rate limiter (max_scale_per_minute) and burst quota accounting. New policy types: "target_utilization" (maintain % GPU utilization), "throughput_guarantee" (min_capacity units guaranteed), and "conservative" (avoid downscales unless sustained). - Burst controls: implement burst_quota per-fleet with configurable window and quota units. Burst consumption is exposed in telemetry and used by scheduler to allow short-term exceed of max_capacity up to quota. - Telemetry: add metrics fleet_utilization_percent, fleet_burst_quota_remaining, fleet_guaranteed_capacity, fleet_scale_events_total and Prometheus rules in telemetry/metrics/fleet_utilization.promql and dashboards in redwood-console. - Console: add AutoscaleConfigForm and fleet utilization panel in console/src/components/dedicated/AutoscaleConfigForm.tsx and console/src/pages/dedicated/FleetOverview.tsx. - CLI/ops: add rollout script scripts/ops/rollout_autoscaling.sh and migration notes in docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md. - Tests: unit tests and integration tests covering policy transitions and burst accounting in go/services/fleet/autoscaler_test.go and integration/e2e/dedicated_autoscale_test.go. Migration: Operators can opt into the new policy by adding autoscaling_policy_v2 to FleetConfig. If unspecified, existing behavior remains unchanged. Backwards compatibility: unchanged API fields still respected; new fields ignored by older controllers. Checklist: - [x] API proto additions (additive) - [x] Controller implementation + unit tests - [x] Burst quota accounting and telemetry - [x] Console UI + basic e2e tests - [x] Docs and rollout script - [x] Performance bench to validate oscillation reduction Commits summary: see commits field for high-level messages. Files changed (high-level): - api/dedicated/v1/autoscaling.proto - go/services/fleet/autoscaler.go - go/services/fleet/autoscaler_test.go - telemetry/metrics/fleet_utilization.promql - console/src/components/dedicated/AutoscaleConfigForm.tsx - console/src/pages/dedicated/FleetOverview.tsx - scripts/ops/rollout_autoscaling.sh - docs/dedicated/autoscaling.md - integration/e2e/dedicated_autoscale_test.go Review notes: initial implementation posted 2026-02-15; reviewers requested clearer safety caps on scaling rate (max_scale_per_minute) and explicit handling of infra failures (fall back to conservative policy). Addressed comments by adding a transient_error_backoff parameter and tests for controller behavior under intermittent API errors. Performance: bench against existing autoscaler on perf-canary showed 37% fewer scale-downs during bursty traffic and 12% lower average tail latency at 95th percentile for small request sizes. Rollout plan: staged rollout using scripts/ops/rollout_autoscaling.sh with canary fleets and 24h observation windows; monitor fleet_scale_events_total, error rates, and price/cost signals. Known limitations: burst_quota is soft and designed for short windows (default 5 minutes); long sustained overcommit is prevented by guaranteed_capacity checks. Related PRs: pr-21012-add-fleet-metrics-exposer (adds base telemetry) and pr-21285-console-fleet-overview.
